units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Presenting Your Research · dialogue line 0
units.source: Today I'd like to share my research topic with everyone.

units.source: Okay, please begin.
units.translation: De acuerdo, puedes comenzar.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Presenting Your Research · dialogue line 2
units.source: My research question is how social media affects teenagers' sleep.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Presenting Your Research · dialogue line 3
units.source: This is a topic with real practical significance.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Presenting Your Research · dialogue line 4
units.source: I used a method combining surveys and interviews.

units.source: How large was the sample size?

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Presenting Your Research · dialogue line 7

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Presenting Your Research · dialogue line 8

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Presenting Your Research · dialogue line 9
units.source: Oh, that's a very valuable finding.
units.translation: Oh, es un hallazgo muy valioso.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Presenting Your Research · grammar (我的研究问题是 + question)
units.source: "我的研究问题是..." ("my research question is...") is the standard academic opener that frames everything that follows in a presentation.
units.translation: «我的研究问题是...» («mi pregunta de investigación es...») es la fórmula académica habitual que enmarca todo lo que sigue en una presentación.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Presenting Your Research · grammar (我的研究问题是 + question)
units.source: Diving into methodology before stating the research question, which leaves the audience without the frame needed to follow the rest of the talk.
units.translation: Entrar directamente en la metodología sin exponer la pregunta de investigación, lo que deja al público sin el marco necesario para seguir el resto de la presentación.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Presenting Your Research · grammar example (我的研究问题是 + question)
units.source: My research question is how social media affects teenagers' sleep.
units.translation: Mi pregunta de investigación es cómo afectan las redes sociales al sueño de los adolescentes.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Presenting Your Research · grammar example (我的研究问题是 + question)
units.source: My research question is how exercise affects sleep quality.
units.translation: Mi pregunta de investigación es cómo afecta el ejercicio a la calidad del sueño.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Presenting Your Research · grammar example (我的研究问题是 + question)
units.source: My research question is how education level affects income.
units.translation: Mi pregunta de investigación es cómo influye el nivel educativo en los ingresos.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Presenting Your Research · grammar (我采用了 + method + 的方法)
units.source: State the research method used in a formal, academic register
units.translation: Indicar el método de investigación empleado con un registro académico formal

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Presenting Your Research · grammar (我采用了 + method + 的方法)
units.source: "我采用了...的方法" ("I used the method of...") is the formal academic way to describe your methodology, more precise than a casual 我用了.
units.translation: «我采用了...的方法» («empleé el método de...») es la forma académica formal de describir la metodología y resulta más precisa que la expresión coloquial 我用了.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Presenting Your Research · grammar (我采用了 + method + 的方法)
units.source: Using the casual 我用了 (I used) instead of the more formal 采用, which sounds underprepared in an academic seminar setting.
units.translation: Usar la expresión coloquial 我用了 («usé») en lugar de la forma más formal 采用, lo que suena poco preparado en un seminario académico.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Presenting Your Research · grammar example (我采用了 + method + 的方法)
units.source: I used a method combining surveys and interviews.
units.translation: Usé un método que combina encuestas y entrevistas.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Presenting Your Research · grammar example (我采用了 + method + 的方法)
units.source: I used an experimental method.
units.translation: Empleé un método experimental.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Presenting Your Research · grammar example (我采用了 + method + 的方法)
units.source: I used a qualitative analysis method.
units.translation: Empleé un método de análisis cualitativo.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Presenting Your Research · grammar (结果表明，+ finding)

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Presenting Your Research · grammar (结果表明，+ finding)
units.source: Present your main research finding formally
units.translation: Presentar formalmente el hallazgo principal de tu investigación

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Presenting Your Research · grammar (结果表明，+ finding)
units.source: "结果表明..." ("the results show...") is the standard academic phrase for presenting a finding, signaling evidence-based conclusions.
units.translation: «结果表明...» («los resultados muestran...») es la fórmula académica habitual para presentar un hallazgo y señala que las conclusiones se basan en evidencia.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Presenting Your Research · grammar (结果表明，+ finding)
units.source: Using the vaguer 我觉得 (I think) to present a data-based finding — 结果表明 correctly signals the claim comes from evidence, not opinion.
units.translation: Usar la expresión más imprecisa 我觉得 («creo») para presentar un hallazgo basado en datos; 结果表明 indica correctamente que la afirmación procede de evidencia y no de una opinión.

units.source: The results show that using a phone before bed significantly shortens sleep duration.
units.translation: Los resultados muestran que usar el teléfono antes de dormir reduce notablemente la duración del sueño.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Fielding a Probing Question · grammar (这是一个很好的问题，+ answer)
units.source: "这是一个很好的问题" ("that's a great question") acknowledges a strong question, giving the presenter a graceful moment to organize their answer.
units.translation: «这是一个很好的问题» («esa es una excelente pregunta») reconoce el valor de una pregunta y le da a quien presenta un momento natural para organizar su respuesta.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Fielding a Probing Question · grammar (这是一个很好的问题，+ answer)
units.source: Answering immediately without this acknowledgment, which can make a difficult question feel rushed or dismissed.
units.translation: Responder de inmediato sin reconocer la pregunta, lo que puede hacer que una pregunta difícil parezca tratada con prisa o desestimada.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Fielding a Probing Question · grammar example (这是一个很好的问题，+ answer)

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Fielding a Probing Question · grammar (您是指 + option A + 还是 + option B？)

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Fielding a Probing Question · grammar (您是指 + option A + 还是 + option B？)
units.source: "您是指...还是...？" ("do you mean...or...?") clarifies an ambiguous question before answering, preventing a mismatched or wasted response.
units.translation: «您是指...还是...？» («¿te refieres a... o a...?») aclara una pregunta ambigua antes de responder y evita dar una respuesta que no corresponda.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Fielding a Probing Question · grammar (您是指 + option A + 还是 + option B？)
units.source: Guessing at the questioner's intent and answering the wrong interpretation — clarifying first avoids a mismatched, wasted answer.
units.translation: Suponer la intención de quien pregunta y responder una interpretación equivocada; pedir una aclaración primero evita una respuesta desacertada e inútil.

units.source: "这确实是一个局限，值得未来深入研究" ("this is indeed a limitation, worth further research") honestly admits a shortcoming while framing it as a direction for future work — standard academic humility.
units.translation: «这确实是一个局限，值得未来深入研究» («esta es, en efecto, una limitación que merece investigarse más») reconoce con sinceridad una debilidad y la presenta como una línea de trabajo futuro, una muestra habitual de humildad académica.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Fielding a Probing Question · grammar (这确实是一个局限，值得 + future direction)
units.source: Being defensive or denying a real limitation exists, which damages credibility far more than honestly acknowledging it.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Citing Sources to Support Claims · grammar (根据以往的研究，+ claim)
units.source: "根据以往的研究..." ("according to previous research...") is the standard academic phrase for grounding a claim in the literature.
units.translation: «根据以往的研究...» («según investigaciones anteriores...») es la fórmula académica habitual para fundamentar una afirmación en la bibliografía.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Citing Sources to Support Claims · grammar (根据以往的研究，+ claim)
units.source: Stating a claim as if it were your own original finding when it's actually drawn from prior literature — proper citation is an academic norm.
units.translation: Presentar como un hallazgo propio y original una afirmación que en realidad procede de bibliografía anterior; citar correctamente es una norma académica.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Citing Sources to Support Claims · grammar example (根据以往的研究，+ claim)
units.source: According to previous research, sleep deprivation affects teenagers' cognitive abilities.
units.translation: Según estudios anteriores, la falta de sueño afecta las capacidades cognitivas de los adolescentes.

units.translation: Según investigaciones anteriores, el estrés afecta la salud.

units.translation: Según investigaciones anteriores, el ejercicio puede mejorar la eficiencia.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Citing Sources to Support Claims · grammar (与 + prior work + 相比，+ comparison)
units.source: Explicitly compare your work to a prior study

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Citing Sources to Support Claims · grammar (与 + prior work + 相比，+ comparison)
units.source: "与前人研究相比" ("compared to prior research") explicitly frames a comparison, situating your findings relative to existing work.
units.translation: «与前人研究相比» («en comparación con investigaciones anteriores») enmarca de forma explícita una comparación y sitúa tus hallazgos respecto al trabajo existente.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Citing Sources to Support Claims · grammar (与 + prior work + 相比，+ comparison)
units.source: Describing your sample or method in isolation without this comparative framing, which loses the context needed to interpret differing results.
units.translation: Describir tu muestra o método de forma aislada, sin este marco comparativo, lo que elimina el contexto necesario para interpretar resultados diferentes.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Citing Sources to Support Claims · grammar (这可能解释了 + comparison + 上的差异)
units.source: Offer a plausible explanation for why results differ from prior work

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Citing Sources to Support Claims · grammar (这可能解释了 + comparison + 上的差异)
units.source: "这可能解释了两者结果上的差异" ("this might explain the difference between the two results") offers a tentative, scholarly explanation for a discrepancy rather than ignoring it.
units.translation: «这可能解释了两者结果上的差异» («esto podría explicar la diferencia entre ambos resultados») plantea una explicación académica y prudente de una discrepancia en lugar de ignorarla.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Citing Sources to Support Claims · grammar (这可能解释了 + comparison + 上的差异)
units.source: Leaving a discrepancy with prior findings unexplained, which weakens the credibility of your own results — offering a plausible cause is expected.
units.translation: Dejar sin explicación una discrepancia respecto a hallazgos anteriores, lo que debilita la credibilidad de tus propios resultados; se espera que propongas una causa plausible.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Discussing Limitations and Future Work · grammar (首先，+ limitation 1。其次，+ limitation 2。)

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Discussing Limitations and Future Work · grammar (首先，+ limitation 1。其次，+ limitation 2。)
units.source: "首先...其次..." ("first...second...") clearly sequences multiple limitations, which is easier for the audience to track than an unordered list.
units.translation: «首先...其次...» («en primer lugar... en segundo lugar...») ordena claramente varias limitaciones y permite que el público las siga mejor que una lista sin orden.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Discussing Limitations and Future Work · grammar (首先，+ limitation 1。其次，+ limitation 2。)
units.source: Listing limitations without sequencing markers, which can make it unclear how many points remain or blur them together.
units.translation: Enumerar limitaciones sin marcadores de orden, lo que puede hacer que no quede claro cuántos puntos faltan o que estos se confundan entre sí.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Discussing Limitations and Future Work · grammar example (首先，+ limitation 1。其次，+ limitation 2。)
units.source: First, the sample only comes from one city, so its representativeness is limited. Second, this study is cross-sectional, so it can't establish causality.
units.translation: En primer lugar, la muestra procede de una sola ciudad, por lo que su representatividad es limitada. En segundo lugar, este es un estudio transversal, por lo que no puede establecer una relación causal.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Discussing Limitations and Future Work · grammar example (首先，+ limitation 1。其次，+ limitation 2。)
units.source: First, there wasn't enough time. Second, the budget was limited.
units.translation: En primer lugar, no hubo tiempo suficiente. En segundo lugar, el presupuesto era limitado.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Discussing Limitations and Future Work · grammar example (首先，+ limitation 1。其次，+ limitation 2。)
units.source: First, the sample was too small. Second, the method had limitations.
units.translation: En primer lugar, la muestra era demasiado pequeña. En segundo lugar, el método tenía limitaciones.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Discussing Limitations and Future Work · grammar (未来可以采用 + method + 来 + purpose)

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Discussing Limitations and Future Work · grammar (未来可以采用 + method + 来 + purpose)
units.source: "未来可以采用...来验证..." ("future research could use...to verify...") proposes a concrete method paired with its purpose, more useful than a vague "more research is needed."
units.translation: «未来可以采用...来验证...» («en el futuro se podría emplear... para comprobar...») propone un método concreto junto con su propósito y resulta más útil que decir vagamente «se necesita investigar más».

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Discussing Limitations and Future Work · grammar (未来可以采用 + method + 来 + purpose)
units.source: Saying only 需要更多研究 (more research is needed) without specifying a method — pairing the method with its purpose is far more actionable.
units.translation: Decir únicamente 需要更多研究 («se necesita investigar más») sin especificar un método; vincular el método con su propósito permite actuar con mucha mayor claridad.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Discussing Limitations and Future Work · grammar example (未来可以采用 + method + 来 + purpose)
units.source: Future research could use a longitudinal design to verify causality.

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Discussing Limitations and Future Work · grammar example (未来可以采用 + method + 来 + purpose)

units.context: Scenario: Academic Seminar Discussion · Lesson: Discussing Limitations and Future Work · grammar example (未来可以采用 + method + 来 + purpose)
